title: Affordability of Rising Public Housing Prices and Impact of Prices on Marriage and Fertility Rates
what_it_is: Affordability of Rising Public Housing Prices and Impact of Prices on Marriage and Fertility Rates

sections.label: Property affordability questions to Minister
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for National Development about measures for property affordability, manpower policy impact on prices, and studies on housing prices and fertility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what measures are being taken to address the growing sentiment that Singapore property market is unaffordable for the masses; (b) how will the recent adjustments to manpower policies impact property prices; and (c) beyond existing cooling measures, what else will the Government do to ensure housing remains affordable for Singaporeans if housing market conditions do not improve.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development whether the Ministry has conducted or will conduct studies on the impact of rising public housing prices on marriage and fertility rates.

sections.label: New 4-room flat prices and grants
sections.summary: Average new 4-room non-mature estate flat prices were $341,000 in 2019 and $348,000 in the first three quarters of this year, with grants up to $80,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The average price for a new 4-room flat in a non-mature estate has remained relatively stable at $341,000 in 2019 and $348,000 in the first three quarters of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Eligible first-timer buyers can also receive Enhanced CPF Housing Grants (EHG) of up to $80,000, with more help for lower-income buyers.

sections.label: Housing loan income share and CPF
sections.summary: After $45,000 in grants, buyers use about 23% of monthly income for housing loan, serviceable from CPF with no cash outlay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: After factoring in the $45,000 in grants they would receive, they will need to use about 23% of their monthly income for their housing loan, which means that they will be able to service their mortgages from their monthly Central Provident Fund (CPF) contributions with no cash outlay.

sections.label: Wait-out period for private property owners
sections.summary: A 15-month wait-out period was introduced before private property owners may purchase a non-subsidised HDB resale flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: First, we introduced a wait-out period of 15 months before private property owners are allowed to purchase a non-subsidised HDB resale flat.

sections.label: Tighter home loan borrowing limits
sections.summary: The medium-term rate floor under TDSR and MSR frameworks was raised from 3.5% to 4% per annum for residential property loans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have thus implemented the following measures to tighten the maximum amount that can be taken for home loans and ensure prudent borrowing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have raised the medium-term rate floor used under the Total Debt Servicing Ratio (TDSR) and MSR frameworks to compute a borrower's maximum loan quantum for residential property loans granted by private financial institutions from 3.5% to 4% per annum.

sections.label: Increased BTO flat supply
sections.summary: HDB ramped up BTO supply and is on track to launch 23,000 flats per year in 2022 and 2023, a 35% increase from 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For HDB, we have ramped up our BTO supply and are on track to launch 23,000 flats per year in 2022 and 2023, or a 35% increase from 2021.

sections.label: Private housing supply and property market
sections.summary: The Confirmed List private housing supply rose 75% from 2021 to 2022, and the Government will intervene to keep the property market stable and public housing affordable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The supply of private housing on the Confirmed List of the Government Land Sales (GLS) programme has also been increased by 75% from 2021 to 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We are prepared to increase supply further to meet the demand for private housing, if needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Government will intervene and do what is necessary, to ensure a stable property market and affordable public housing for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will do so decisively but also carefully, being cognisant of the uncertain global economic outlook and rising interest rates environment, which will affect home prices and contribute to uncertainty in our property market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will continue to monitor the market closely and adjust our policies as necessary on both housing demand and supply, to ensure that prices move broadly in line with economic fundamentals.

sections.label: BTO quota for first-timer families
sections.summary: The quota of 3-room and 4-room BTO flats in non-mature estates set aside for first-timer families was increased to 85% and 95% respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The quota of 3-room and 4-room BTO flats in non-mature estates set aside for first-timer families, was increased to 85% and 95% respectively.

sections.label: Enhanced CPF housing grant
sections.summary: Eligible first-timer buyers of new flats can enjoy an enhanced CPF housing grant of up to $80,000, on top of subsidies in new flat prices.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Eligible first-timer buyers who buy new flats can enjoy an enhanced CPF housing grant of up to $80,000, on top of the generous subsidies in new flat prices.

sections.label: November BTO launch and flat supply
sections.summary: Home buyers can look forward to 9,500 flats in the upcoming November BTO launch, and up to 100,000 new flats are to be launched from 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We are well on track this year and home buyers can look forward to 9,500 flats being offered in the upcoming November BTO launch exercise.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We are prepared to launch up to 100,000 new flats from 2021 to 2025.

sections.label: 100,000 flats and other housing sources
sections.summary: The 100,000 flats, if demand persists, will meet much of this demand, but HDB BTO flats are not the only source of housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The 100,000 flats, if the demand persists, will be able to meet much of this demand, but remember that HDB BTO flats are not the only source of housing.

sections.label: Studies on housing, marriage and fertility
sections.summary: No studies were conducted on housing prices' impact on marriage and fertility rates, but regular surveys and engagements indicate many couples aspire to own a home before starting a family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Then, the second was, he had asked – because he said I had not answered – whether any studies are done.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I had earlier said, while we have not conducted studies on the impact of housing prices on marriage and fertility rates, our regular surveys and engagements indicate that many couples continue to aspire to have their own home before they start a family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, it means we have not conducted studies, but we have done regular surveys and engagements which give us the indications that we need.
